museum.lineage: Oberon (Ceres, 1987) → Oberon System 3 / Gadgets → Native Oberon (PC, 1996–2003) → Bluebottle / A2
museum.arch: i386, on bare PC hardware (no host OS)
museum.blurb: Niklaus Wirth and Jürg Gutknecht's Oberon: an entire operating system, compiler and tiling text desktop written by two people, where every word on screen is a command you execute with the middle mouse button — here as ETH's 1999 Native Oberon on a bare PC.
museum.notes: Live streamhost station. Native Oberon 2.3.6 boots from its own IDE partition (no host OS) into the System 3 Gadgets desktop at 1280x1024; the System.Tool text on the right is the menu: middle-click any command word (Ctrl+click on a two-button mouse) to run it, left-click to place the caret and type. Relative PS/2 pointer through the daemon's rel bridge (1.5 px per unit measured). disk.qcow2 is the single block device and carries the golden vmstate.

emulator.source: /opt/qemu-oberon — fork c5449c80 (github.com/Wnt/qemu, branch kernel-hive) plus the point32le_yx / point16le_yup layouts added to qemu-patch 0007 kh-ramabs; machine type pc-i440fx-11.0

reset.mouse: PASS 1:1 absolute: kh-ramabs writes Native Oberon's own pointer coordinate (two LONGINTs at guest-physical 0x140160, order y-then-x with y counted up from the bottom -- layout point32le_yx) and nudges PS/2 by one unit to republish it. Five targets (20,20) (1250,20) (20,1000) (1250,1000) (640,512) on the 1280x1024 surface, TWO laps with a move to (300,700) between every target: the guest's own words and the device's read-back are EXACT at all ten, and the sprite located in the framebuffer is within 1 px (worst |dx|,|dy| = 1,1 -- the diff locator's own background-dependent edge column, not pointer error). A middle click at (855,630) on System.Directory opened a Directory viewer. Nudge stays at 1 unit = 1 px: Oberon accelerates to 1.5 px/unit at 6 units and up.
